ratings.label: Feasible
ratings.desc: Runs into neither the Constitution nor EU law; an ordinary law, a decree or affordable money is enough.

ratings.label: Hard
ratings.desc: Possible, but needs something difficult: an organic law (176 votes), the regions' consent, a large sum of money, or years.

ratings.label: Unlikely
ratings.desc: Serious obstacles: the courts, EU law, regional powers, a cost the budget cannot carry, or no majority.

ratings.label: Not possible as things stand
ratings.desc: Conflicts with the Constitution or EU law, or needs a constitutional reform with no chance of the three-fifths or two-thirds majority.

ratings.label: Vague
ratings.desc: No figures, deadline or mechanism, so delivery cannot be checked.

housing.label: Tax breaks for landlords instead of caps
Tax or restrict large owners and investors
Limit who can buy or get housing

taxes.label: Taxes on capital, wealth and big firms

parties.name: PP
parties.summary: Taken one by one, almost every item is feasible, but the programme does not add up as a whole: income tax indexation, 4% VAT, zero contributions and an end to the generation tax sit next to 4,500 more doctors, 50% state funding for long-term care, €40 billion for water and lower debt.
parties.doable: Most measures need only an ordinary law or a decree, and many extend schemes that already exist, such as the ICO deposit guarantee.
parties.limits: The weakest points are the million homes (Spain now completes about 100,000 a year), a €300 billion infrastructure plan, and repealing the amnesty, which cannot be undone where it has already been applied (art. 9.3 of the Constitution).

parties.name: PSOE
parties.summary: The party is in government and mostly continues what it has started, so its ratings are high. The programme does not address the main question for the next government: Catalonia and the conditions set by ERC and Junts.
parties.doable: Many items extend measures already under way: the minimum wage at 60% of the average wage, contributions for the self-employed based on real income, CASA 47.
parties.limits: Constitutional reforms (housing, pensions, the Senate, *aforamientos*) are impossible without PP; the 37.5-hour week has already failed in Congress; the €83 billion regional debt write-off is an organic law without a guaranteed 176 votes; "1% of GDP for housing" and +€21 billion for the regions have no stated source.

parties.name: Vox
parties.summary: The core of the programme is "national priority" (*prioridad nacional*) in housing, the minimum income, schools and benefits, a tax on remittances, "remigration", leaving EU climate rules, and Gibraltar. Almost a quarter of items have no figures.
parties.doable: What overlaps with PP is feasible: judges electing judges to the CGPJ, repealing the Housing Law and the Democratic Memory Law, Criminal Code changes.
parties.limits: Most of the core conflicts with art. 14 of the Constitution and with EU law, and Gibraltar cannot be settled without the UK's consent.

parties.name: Sumar
parties.summary: The most expensive programme: 1% of GDP for housing, 2.3% of GDP for the regions, 3.5% for climate, 7% for education, 8% for health, €200 per child. Together that is over €100 billion a year, more than the new taxes would raise.
parties.doable: Tax changes by ordinary law (a 20% minimum corporate tax, a wider wealth tax) and practical steps for migrants, such as easier registration and a basic bank account.
parties.limits: Expropriating homes from large owners, banning purchases not for one's own use and nationalising the grids run into art. 33 of the Constitution and EU law.

parties.name: Podemos
parties.summary: The most D ratings of any party (15): a 40% rent cut, a ban on buying homes not for one's own use, a republic and an end to the King's immunity, neutrality. Leaving NATO, a universal basic income, retirement at 63 and a 30-hour week are blocked by money and the lack of a majority (C) rather than by law.
parties.doable: Targeted measures: bringing seasonal lets under rental law, abolishing the Beckham regime, lower VAT on services, paid internships.
parties.limits: The flagship housing measures conflict with property rights (art. 33) and EU free movement of capital.

parties.name: ERC
parties.summary: What is realistic is bargaining inside a PSOE-led government: the FLA debt write-off, Rodalies trains, the "gag law" (*ley mordaza*).
parties.doable: Items that pass through a Congress deal: debt relief, transfer of commuter rail, tax changes on capital and tourist lets.
parties.limits: A referendum, a Basque-style funding agreement, a Catalan minimum wage and transfers of immigration and rental powers run into art. 149 of the Constitution and Constitutional Court rulings.

parties.name: Junts
parties.summary: Economically right-of-centre (no rent caps, deductions, tax breaks), but its main demands are territorial: an economic agreement, social security, the Schengen border, the Catalan high court as last instance.
parties.doable: Tax relief and rental supply incentives by ordinary law.
parties.limits: The Constitution largely rules out the territorial demands (Constitutional Court, 2010 ruling on the Statute).

parties.name: EH Bildu
parties.summary: Realistic social measures (rent stability, action on tourist flats) sit next to recognition of nations and a right to self-determination, leaving NATO and scrapping EU fiscal rules.
parties.doable: Rental rules by ordinary law, such as automatic renewal and caps on annual rent updates.
parties.limits: Recognition of nations and self-determination, a regional minimum wage and scrapping fiscal rules are impossible without constitutional reform.

parties.name: PNV
parties.summary: The most pragmatic of the regional programmes. Most items implement the Gernika Statute and the *concierto*, which also moved forward under Sánchez.
parties.doable: Tax tweaks within EU rules, pension measures and Statute transfers agreed in joint commissions.
parties.limits: Recognition of a "nation" and a separate Basque minimum wage are not feasible.

parties.name: BNG
parties.summary: A short programme of 10 commitments with few figures. Realistic social measures sit next to recognition of Galicia as a nation, leaving NATO and a regional minimum wage.
parties.doable: Tenant protection and limits on tourist and seasonal lets.
parties.limits: Nationhood and self-determination need constitutional reform; the pension and working-week pledges lack money or a majority.

parties.name: CC
parties.summary: Almost all demands are about money and carrying out the Statute and the islands' tax regime (*REF*): the usual bargaining for a vote in Congress.
parties.doable: Island tax breaks, the 75% resident travel discount and holiday-let rules, mostly extending what exists.
parties.limits: The one contested point: limiting home purchases by foreigners, which EU law does not allow for EU citizens.
